title: Finding your way

fn.en: Ask how to get somewhere and explain the way to someone else.

useful: Excuse me, is there a … near here?

sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which words say WHERE something is, and which say HOW you move?

items.q: The chemist is ___ the bank and the library.
items.why: between / opposite / behind say where something IS.  along / past / through say how you MOVE.

items.q: Go ___ the café and then turn right.
Walk ___ this street to the end.
Go ___ the park — it’s faster than going round it.
The car park is ___ the building, not at the front.

items.why: turn into a street; turn left / right with no preposition after it.

use: Could you give me some directions, please?
tts: Excuse me, could you give me some directions, please? — Yes, of course! How can I help you?
Thanks! So, is there a chemist near here? — Yes, there is. It’s in the town centre.
How do I get there? — OK, well, go out of the main door and turn left. Then go to the end of the road and turn left again.
Go straight on for about five minutes. Go past the internet café and the bank, and then turn left into Raya Street.

acts.title: Two ways to the station
text: The short way: go out of the hotel and turn right. Walk along the main street for five minutes and go past the library. Cross the road at the traffic lights. The station is on your left, opposite the post office.
The nice way: turn left instead. Go through the park — there’s a small lake in the middle — and take the second turning on the right. The station is behind the big white building on the corner.
The short way takes six minutes. The nice way takes fifteen, but nobody who takes it complains.

On the nice way you take the first turning on the right.

write.q: Write directions from your home to the nearest shop: 6 steps. Use turn, go straight on, go past, cross and one preposition of place (opposite, between, behind or on the corner).
write.ph: Go out of my building and…
write.model: Go out of my building and turn right. Go straight on for about three minutes. Go past the school and cross the road at the traffic lights. Take the second turning on the left. The shop is on the corner, opposite a small café. It’s behind the bus stop, so you can’t see it at first.

speak.q: Ask for two places out loud, then give directions to one place near you. Use at least four direction phrases.
speak.model: Excuse me, is there a chemist near here? How do I get to the station? — Go straight on to the lights, cross the road, then take the first turning on the right. It’s on the left, opposite the bank.
